questions.q: How much free push does a rocket get from Earth’s spin when it launches due east from Sriharikota, and from the equator?
questions.do: Click Sriharikota under Why near the equator? and read Free push from Earth’s spin. Then click Kourou.
questions.a: About 452 m/s from Sriharikota (13.7° N) and 463 m/s from Kourou (5° N). At the equator itself it is 465 m/s, the speed the ground moves as Earth spins.

questions.q: Why does a satellite launched from Baikonur need a bigger push to reach geostationary orbit than one launched from Kourou?
questions.do: Compare Extra over a launch from the equator for Baikonur and Kourou, and look at the orange curve.
questions.a: A rocket cannot easily reach an orbit tilted less than its site’s latitude. From Baikonur (46°) the orbit starts tilted 46°, and untilting it at the top of the transfer orbit costs several hundred m/s more than from Kourou (5°).

questions.q: Which country launched the most rockets this year, and how many launches were there in all?
questions.do: Read This year so far and the country chart.
questions.a: The United States, then China. The totals are refreshed daily, so read the current numbers on the page (274 launches by 18 November 2026, about one every 28 hours).

questions.q: Which Indian rocket that is not ISRO’s flew from Sriharikota in 2026?
questions.a: Vikram-I, built by the private company Skyroot Aerospace, on a successful demonstration flight in July 2026.

questions.q: When did the first satellite reach orbit, and what was it?
questions.do: Read the introduction at the top of the page.
questions.a: Sputnik 1, launched by the Soviet Union on 4 October 1957.
